collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two elders)

collection.description: Two elders hold their yearly tall tale contest by the fire: answer with a bigger fish, or a smaller one.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Once a year, (subject) and (friend) hold a contest of tall tales by the fire. Everyone knows the stories are made up; that's the whole point. Tonight (subject) has told of a fish so big it had its own island. Now (friend) is on (friend.his/her) feet, ready to answer.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) tells of a fish so big that the island was on IT, and that they are all living on its back right now. The crowd roars. (subject) stands up: that fish was (subject)'s cousin. It goes on until the fire burns low and the children are asleep in grown-ups' laps. Nobody declares a winner. Nobody ever does.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) tells, in a solemn whisper, of a fish so small that it lived in a single drop of water, and once got lost in a raindrop for a whole season. The crowd goes quiet, then delighted. (subject) concedes. "Small," (subject.he/she) mutters. "Never thought of small." Next year (subject.he/she) comes back with a fish so small it's invisible.
